blocks.text: Technology has reshaped banking, and computerisation of bank business has become a top priority. As per the 2024-25 syllabus material, Indian banking institutions have already crossed the **70% level of computerisation** of their business.

blocks.title: Automated Teller Machine (ATM)
rows: A computerised machine that lets a bank customer reach their account, withdraw cash and do other financial and non-financial transactions **without visiting the branch**.
Cash deposit, cash withdrawal, mini statement, balance enquiry, money transfer, bill payment and more.

blocks.title: Plastic money
blocks.text: Credit cards are popularly called **plastic money**. Smart, debit, prepaid and credit cards are all non-cash (cashless) payment products.

blocks.title: ATM varieties by location and ownership
rows: Inside the branch premises or very close to the branch.
Away from the branch, in places such as malls, petrol pumps and railway stations.
Inside an organisation's premises, generally only for its employees.
Set up, owned and operated by **non-bank entities**. They are authorised by the RBI under the **Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007**. Cash deposit is **not permitted** at a WLA.
Hardware is owned and maintained by a service provider, but **cash management and connectivity** to the banking network come from a sponsor bank whose brand the ATM carries.

Has an ATM-type interface plus at least one biometric capture device (fingerprint scanner, iris camera, palm or finger-vein scanner, face-recognition camera). Also called multi-biometric or wall-mount biometric ATMs.
An ATM mounted on a vehicle that moves between locations.

blocks.title: First White Label ATM
blocks.text: India's first white label ATM was launched by **Tata** under the brand name **IndiCash**.

blocks.title: White vs Brown label ATM
blocks.phrase: White = Without a bank (owner is a non-bank). Brown = Borrowed bank brand and cash.
letters: Owned and run by a non-bank company; no cash deposits allowed
Service provider owns the machine; sponsor bank supplies cash, network and brand
Onsite = near the branch; Offsite = malls, pumps, stations; Worksite = staff only
blocks.note: If a question says 'non-bank entity owns and operates', the answer is always White Label.

blocks.title: How an ATM hands out notes
items: An ATM holds **cassettes**, each configured for one note denomination (the source lists ₹2,000, ₹500, ₹200 and ₹100).
Each cassette has an electronic setting at the back end, so when it is docked the machine knows which denomination it carries.
A software setting then decides the mix of notes. For a ₹3,000 withdrawal the machine may pick one ₹2,000 note and the rest in ₹500, ₹200 or ₹100 notes, depending on the logic the bank builds in.
Banks usually decide this dispensing logic.

blocks.title: ATM numbers (as per the 2024-25 book; these change)
rows: Over 2,00,000 ATMs across the country at the time of writing.
**NCR Corporation India** with a **47% market share** and almost 1 lakh machines.
ICICI Bank 16,544; Axis Bank 16,400; HDFC Bank 18,522 (as per March 2022).

blocks.title: Dated numbers
blocks.text: Machine counts keep changing. Exams usually ask only who is **largest** (SBI), not the exact figure. Note too that ₹2,000 notes were withdrawn from circulation by the RBI in 2023, so cassettes now mainly carry the other denominations.

blocks.title: Credit card vs debit card
rows: Plastic card issued by a bank so you can pay a merchant, promising to repay the issuer the amount plus agreed charges
Money is borrowed; you repay later
Account is debited immediately or on the same day the card is used

blocks.title: Rules for banks issuing credit cards
items: **Central Bank of India** was the first public sector bank to introduce a credit card.
A bank can run credit card business **departmentally** or through a **subsidiary** company set up for the purpose.
It can also enter a **tie-up** with another bank that already issues credit cards (for domestic business).
**Prior RBI approval is not needed**; the bank's own Board approval is enough.
Only banks with a **net worth of ₹100 crore or more** should undertake credit card business.

blocks.title: Do not mix up the two
blocks.text: In a **debit card** the money leaves your own account at once, so there is no credit period. In a **credit card** you spend the bank's money first and pay later.

blocks.title: Other card types
rows: Works like a gift card: you load money and can spend only up to that amount. Used by travellers for holiday money and by people without a normal bank account, such as kids, teens or people with poor credit ratings.

Holds an electronic **chip that stores cash**; ideal for small payments such as bus fares and coffee bills. No identification, signature or authorisation is needed, the exact amount is deducted by a card-reading machine, and **no change** is given.

A credit card issued by a card company that has tied up with a popular brand for exclusive benefits. Example: the **Citi-Times** card gives Citibank card benefits plus discounts on Times Music items and free entry to Times Music events.

blocks.title: Which card does what
blocks.phrase: Credit = Climb now, pay later. Debit = Deduct now. Prepaid = Preloaded. Smart = chip Stores cash.
letters: Borrow first, repay later with charges
Account is deducted immediately; no credit period
Pre-loaded amount like a gift card
Chip stores cash for small payments; no change returned

blocks.text: **RuPay** is the Indian version of a card network, started by the **National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) on 26 March 2012**. The name is a blend of **Rupee** and **Payment**. It mainly provides **debit cards** and also issues **Kisan Credit Cards** for farmers.

items: RuPay competes with **MasterCard, Visa and Amex** in India.
As per the 2024-25 book, RuPay held over **36%** of the Indian card payment market, behind **Visa** which had over **50%**.
India is the **sixth country** in the world with a domestic payment gateway system; the other five are the **US, Japan, China, Singapore and Brazil**.

blocks.title: RuPay in one line
blocks.text: RuPay = Rupee + Payment, launched by NPCI on 26 March 2012, mainly debit cards, and India was the sixth country with a domestic card scheme.

The **Kisan Credit Card** was introduced by the NDA Government in **August 1998** as a hassle-free, timely way to meet the production credit needs of farmers. It was first announced in the **Budget 1998-99** by then Finance Minister **Yashwant Sinha**. **NABARD** later prepared a Model KCC Scheme with the major banks, based on the recommendations of the **R V Gupta Committee**.

blocks.title: KCC at a glance
rows: Five years, subject to annual renewals
Allied activities such as pump sets, land development, plantation, drip irrigation
Crop loans and working capital given as a revolving cash credit limit, repayable in 12 months
Within a maximum of 5 years, depending on activity, investment and repayment capacity
Commercial banks, RRBs and cooperatives across the country

blocks.title: KCC facts: the 98 Sinha Gupta trick
blocks.phrase: 1998: Sinha announced it, Gupta shaped it, NABARD wrote the model.
letters: Prepared the Model KCC Scheme with banks
blocks.note: Validity is 5 years; cash credit repayable in 12 months; term loan within 5 years.

rows: A computerised replacement for a cash register that can process credit and debit cards. The customer enters the card **PIN** to complete the transaction. Cards are swiped at this terminal in a merchant's store.
**Electronic Funds Transfer at Point of Sale**: an electronic payment system built on payment cards (**debit or credit**) used at payment terminals located at points of sale.

blocks.text: EFTPOS covers **both** debit and credit cards, so an answer saying 'only debit cards' is wrong.

sections.title: ATM insurance, cardless cash and CDM

blocks.title: ATM insurance policy
items: ATM cardholders of both public and private sector banks are eligible for **accidental hospitalisation cover** and **accidental death cover** from the card issuing bank.
The cover ranges from **₹50,000 to ₹20 lakh**.
It cannot be claimed on an **inoperative account**.

It is claimed that a bank account holder using an ATM card gets accidental insurance **without any fee**, and that if someone dies within **45 days** of using the card the family can claim the amount.

blocks.title: Cardless cash ('Cash-on-Mobile')
items: Lets you withdraw cash from an ATM **without an ATM or debit card**, through a newly launched mobile banking application.
The service is **free of cost**.
The app also enables intra-bank mobile-to-mobile and mobile-to-account transfers and NEFT; **IMPS** is part of it.
Withdrawal limit through Cash-on-Mobile: up to **₹5,000 per day**.

blocks.title: Cash Deposit Machine (CDM)
rows: An ATM-like machine that lets customers deposit cash straight into their account using the ATM-cum-debit card; credit is instant and the receipt shows the updated balance.
PIN change, balance enquiry and mini statement

blocks.title: New banking services through ATMs
items: Before 14 Jan 2016

Banks could offer only RBI-approved services: deposits and withdrawals, PIN change, cheque book request, statement, balance enquiry, fund transfer, bill payments, railway tickets, and products such as loans, insurance and credit cards.
RBI allowed banks to offer **all their banking products and services** through ATMs, provided their technology supports it.

blocks.text: With effect from **1 November 2014**, banks must give savings bank account holders a minimum number of free ATM transactions every month, as shown below (the figures are as per the book; RBI has revised the rules since).

blocks.title: Minimum free transactions per month
rows: Other banks' ATMs in the six metros (Mumbai, New Delhi, Chennai, Kolkata, Bengaluru, Hyderabad)
Other banks' ATMs in non-metro locations

items: Beyond the free limit a customer can be charged a maximum of **₹20 per transaction** (plus service tax, if any) in the book's version of the rule.
For a **failed ATM transaction**, RBI rules require the bank to re-credit the money within 7 working days; beyond that the bank must pay **₹100 per day** as compensation to the customer.

blocks.title: Free ATM trips: 5 - 3 - 5
blocks.phrase: Own bank 5, Metro other bank 3, Non-metro other bank 5. Only the metro slot is 3.
letters: Other banks' ATMs in the six metros
Other banks' ATMs outside the metros
blocks.note: Six metros: Mumbai, New Delhi, Chennai, Kolkata, Bengaluru, Hyderabad.

blocks.title: MICR (Magnetic Ink Character Recognition)
rows: Technology that lets machines read and process cheques, handling thousands of cheques in a short time.
First 3 digits = **city** code, next 3 = **bank** code, last 3 = **branch** code.

blocks.title: Reading MICR 110211001 (Axis Bank, Delhi)
items: City code: New Delhi
Bank code: Axis Bank
Branch code: Parliament Street

blocks.title: IFSC (Indian Financial System Code)
rows: NEFT, RTGS and the Centralised Funds Management System (CFMS).
First 4 characters = the bank/entity; fifth character is a **0 (zero)** kept for future use; last 6 characters = the branch.

blocks.title: SWIFT code
rows: A unique identification code for financial and non-financial institutions, approved by the **International Organization for Standardization (ISO)**; registration is handled by **SWIFT Standards**, a division of the Society for Worldwide Interbank Financial Telecommunication.
Moving money between banks, especially **international wire transfers**, and exchanging other messages between banks.

blocks.title: Code lengths: 9, 11, 8-or-11
blocks.phrase: MICR is a Nine-digit cheque code, IFSC is Eleven with a Zero in the middle, SWIFT is Eight or Eleven for the world.
blocks.note: Domestic transfer (NEFT/RTGS) = IFSC. International wire transfer = SWIFT. Cheque clearing = MICR.

blocks.title: Which code for which job
blocks.text: IFSC is for **NEFT, RTGS and CFMS**, SWIFT is for **international wire transfers**, and MICR is for **cheque processing**. Questions love swapping them.

**Electronic Clearing Service (ECS)** is offered by the RBI for faster payments and collections. It suits transactions that are **repetitive and periodic**, meaning they recur after a fixed interval. Institutions use it for **bulk payments** or **bulk collections**, and they can start the process without visiting a branch again and again.

blocks.title: Bulk payment vs bulk collection under ECS
rows: Water bills, cess and tax collections
Loan instalment repayments, periodic mutual fund investments, insurance premium

blocks.title: RTGS vs NEFT vs IMPS
rows: **Gross** settlement, instruction by instruction, in real time
Minimum ₹2 lakh; the source also quotes a ₹10 lakh maximum, but RBI has no upper ceiling and banks may set their own limit
Instant transfer using the mobile phone
Limits are set by each bank; for example SBI allowed only one beneficiary per calendar day

blocks.title: Gross vs Net
blocks.text: RTGS = **gross** (each instruction settled individually, real time, large value). NEFT = **net** (batch based, deferred). Real time gross settlement benefits customers and banks alike.

blocks.title: RTGS or NEFT?
blocks.phrase: RTGS = Rich and Rapid (big amounts, one by one). NEFT = Net and Neat batches (no limits).
letters: RTGS: real time, gross, large value (min ₹2 lakh)
NEFT: net settlement in batches, no minimum or maximum

blocks.text: **Mobile banking (M-banking)** goes a step beyond internet and tele-banking: you can transact without even making a phone call, making it truly **'Any Time, Any Where' banking**. It works through text messages and offers two broad kinds of service.

blocks.title: Types of mobile banking service
rows: Help the customer keep track of activity on their accounts.
Let the customer ask for information about their accounts and transactions.

blocks.title: Internet banking (net banking)
items: Lets a customer do many banking activities online, anywhere in the world with internet access.
**Fund transfers** can be made between accounts, across branches and cities, even to an account in any other bank. The customer only needs to submit a **signed declaration** to use this facility.

Utility bills (telephone, mobile, electricity) can be paid online. Some banks restrict requests for new fixed deposits or demand drafts to regular banking hours; a request made after hours is executed on the **next working day**.

blocks.title: Related ideas
blocks.text: **Tele-banking** is based on **voice banking**. **Mobile banking** is seen as the best branch-alternative for **financial inclusion**. Having **100% CBS** means all branches run on **core banking solutions**.

blocks.title: Key terms
rows: A digital representation of value that works as a medium of exchange, a unit of account and/or a store of value, but **does not have legal tender status** in any jurisdiction.
A type of virtual currency that uses **cryptography** to validate and secure transactions recorded on a **distributed ledger** such as a **blockchain**.
Virtual currency with an equivalent value in real currency, or one that acts as a substitute for real currency.
An example of a convertible virtual currency; it can be traded between users and bought for, or exchanged into, US dollars, euros and other real or virtual currencies.

blocks.title: A Bitcoin transaction (Rob pays Laura)
items: Rob opens his wallet
Scans Laura's address
Enter amount and fee
Then send the payment
Wallet signs it
Uses Rob's private key
Network validates
Nodes propagate and check it
Miners add to a block
Mining = computing a certain hash
Proof of Work solved
Miner broadcasts the new block
Nodes verify the block
And pass it on
Laura sees confirmations
More appear with each new block

blocks.title: Virtual currencies in India
items: Nov 2017
A high-level **Inter-Ministerial Committee** was constituted to study virtual currency issues and propose action.

The Committee submitted its report: it recommended that **all private cryptocurrencies be banned** (except any issued by the State) and that related activity be criminalised through a law. It also suggested a **Standing Committee** to revisit the issues as technology evolves.

blocks.title: Crypto in India: 17-19
blocks.phrase: Committee formed in Seventeen, report in Nineteen: 'ban private crypto, keep State-issued'.
letters: Ban private cryptocurrencies, except any issued by the State

revision: ATM = machine for cash withdrawal and other transactions without visiting the branch; computerisation of banks has crossed 70% as per the book.
White Label ATMs are set up, owned and run by non-banks under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007; cash deposit is not allowed. First WLA: Tata's IndiCash.
Brown label = provider owns machine, sponsor bank provides cash and connectivity; Onsite/Offsite/Worksite depend on location.
NCR Corporation India is the leading ATM player (47% share); SBI has the largest bank ATM network.
Central Bank of India was the first public bank to introduce a credit card; banks need no RBI approval but need a net worth of ₹100 crore or more.
Debit card: account debited immediately, no credit period. Smart card: chip stores cash, no change given. Citi-Times is a co-branded card.
RuPay (Rupee + Payment) was launched by NPCI on 26 March 2012; India is the sixth country with a domestic payment gateway.
Kisan Credit Card: August 1998, Yashwant Sinha, R V Gupta Committee; valid 5 years; cash credit repayable in 12 months, term loan within 5 years.
ATM insurance ranges from ₹50,000 to ₹20 lakh; Cash-on-Mobile lets you withdraw up to ₹5,000 a day without a card.
CDM: ₹49,900 per transaction, up to 200 notes; on 14 January 2016 RBI allowed all banking services through ATMs.
Free ATM transactions: 5 at own bank, 3 at other banks in six metros, 5 at other banks elsewhere; excess charge capped at ₹20 in the book.
MICR = 9 digits (city, bank, branch); IFSC = 11 characters (4 bank + 0 + 6 branch); SWIFT/BIC = 8 or 11 characters.
ECS is for repetitive, periodic bulk payments (salary, pension, interest) and bulk collections (bills, EMIs, premiums).
RTGS: gross, real-time, minimum ₹2 lakh. NEFT: deferred net batches, no limit. IMPS: instant via mobile.
Virtual currency has no legal tender status; the 2017-19 Inter-Ministerial Committee recommended banning private cryptocurrencies.
